record.original_question: For a large positive integer N, what is the largest size of a subset of the interval [1; N], free of three-term arithmetic progressions? The present records are due to Behrend (who constructed in a progression-free set A [1; N], satisfying jAj > N exp( cplog N) with an absolute constant c > 0) and Bourgain (who proved in that if A [1; N] is progression-free, then jAj < CN p log log N= log N with an absolute constant C). Narrow the gap between these estimates.

evidence.quote: Dense progression-free integer sets. For a large positive integer N, what is the largest size of a subset of the interval [1; N], free of three-term arithmetic progressions? The present records are due to Behrend (who constructed in [6] a progression-free set A [1; N], satisfying jAj > N exp( cplog N) with an absolute constant c > 0) and Bourgain (who proved in [11] that if A [1; N] is progression-free, then jAj < CN p log log N= log N with an absolute constant C). Narrow the gap between these estimates.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $r_3(N)$ denote the largest cardinality of a subset $A \subseteq \{1, 2, \ldots, N\}$ that contains no three-term arithmetic progression, i.e., no triple $(a, a+d, a+2d)$ with $a \in A$, $a+d \in A$, $a+2d \in A$, and $d \neq 0$. It is known that there exist absolute constants $c > 0$ and $C > 0$ such that, for all sufficiently large positive integers $N$,
$$N \exp\!\big(-c\sqrt{\log N}\,\big) \;<\; r_3(N) \;<\; C\,N\,\sqrt{\frac{\log\log N}{\log N}}.$$
Determine the true asymptotic behavior of $r_3(N)$, narrowing the gap between the lower bound (of Behrend type) and the upper bound (of Bourgain type). In particular, decide whether $r_3(N) = N \exp\!\big(-(\log N)^{1/2 + o(1)}\big)$.
artifact.status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made on the upper bound but the problem remains open. Bloom–Sisask (2020) gave the first bound of the form $N/(\log N)^{1+c}$, and in 2023 Kelley and Meka proved $r_3(N) \le N \exp(-c(\log N)^{\beta})$ for an absolute $\beta > 0$ (refined to roughly $\beta = 1/9$ by Bloom–Sisask), which is qualitatively close to Behrend's lower bound $N \exp(-c\sqrt{\log N})$. The exact asymptotic rate, in particular whether Behrend's construction is asymptotically optimal, is still unresolved; a recent (2024) improvement of Behrend's construction has also appeared.

status_evidence.title: The Kelley–Meka bounds for sets free of three-term arithmetic progressions
status_evidence.snippet: Kelley and Meka proved that subsets of {1,...,N} of density at least exp(-c(log N)^{1/12}) contain non-trivial three-term APs, nearly matching Behrend.
status_evidence.claim: Upper bound for r_3(N) was dramatically improved in 2023 to nearly match Behrend's lower bound.

status_evidence.title: Absolutely Sensational Morning News – Kelley and Meka
status_evidence.snippet: Kelley–Meka achieved quasi-polynomial / Behrend-type upper bounds for sets without 3-term arithmetic progressions.
status_evidence.claim: The upper bound has been brought to within a polynomial in the exponent of Behrend's lower bound, but exact asymptotic remains open.

status_evidence.title: Improving Behrend's construction: Sets without arithmetic progressions
status_evidence.snippet: Recent paper improving the constant in Behrend's lower-bound construction for progression-free sets.
status_evidence.claim: Lower bound construction has also been refined recently, indicating ongoing research.
